# Objective

The objective of this file is to create a data entry files to run the Biotic Ligand Model (BLM) desktop version.

We'll be creating 2 BLM data entry files for each trace element:

-   BLM_Data_Entry_for_Zn.xlsx

-   BLM_Data_Entry_for_Cu.xlsx

These files will be used for running BLM as a closed-system (input DIC) in Speciation and Toxicity prediction modes.

See BLM_manual.pdf to learn how to use the BLM.

The BLM requires the following variables to run:

-   Site Name

-   Sample Name

-   Temperature (C)

-   pH

-   Metal concentration (ug/L)

-   Dissolved organic carbon concentration (DOC mg C/L)

-   Humic acid (HA %)

-   Calcium concentration (Ca mg/L)

-   Magnesium concentration (Mg mg/L)

-   Sodium concentration (Na mg/L)

-   Potassium concentration (K mg/L)

-   Sulfate concentration (SO4 mg/L)

-   Chloride concentration (Cl mg/L)

-   Alkalinity as dissolved inorganic carbon concentration (DIC mg/L)

-   Sulfur concentration (S mg/L): under development, but must enter an arbitrary small quantity

We will be obtaining these variables from the WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Final.xlsx file.

## 2. Omitting Samples

Samples will be omitted which do not have all BLM input variables.

Missing sample measurements are denoted with -9999 values.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

vars <- c(
  "Temp_C","Zn_uM","Cu_uM","DOC_uM","Ca_uM","Mg_uM",
  "Na_uM","K_uM","SO4_uM","Cl_uM","DIC_uM"
)

missing_dat <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(vars), ~ .x == -9999)) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Site, all_of(vars))

missing_dat
```

Summarize missing sample measurements

```{r}
# Number of affected samples
n_missing <- nrow(missing_dat)

# Variables most affected
variable_counts <- colSums(missing_dat[vars] == -9999, na.rm = TRUE)

n_missing # total numer of samples with at least 1 missing variable measurement
variable_counts # number of missing values by variable
```

Remove these from the WaDE_Synoptic_Summary

```{r}
WaDE_Synoptic_Summary <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary %>%
  filter(!if_any(all_of(vars), ~ .x == -9999))

# Count number of samples leftover
n_samples <- nrow(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary)
n_samples
```

Build a summary table and export to Excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# 1. Create a new Excel workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# 2. Add a worksheet called "Filtered Samples"
addWorksheet(wb, "Filtered Samples")

# 3. Make a small summary table of your counts
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Total unique samples before filtering",
    "Samples with missing values of BLM vars",
    "Samples remaining after filtering"
  ),
  Value = c(n_total, n_missing, n_samples)
)

# 4. Make a table for the number of -9999 values per variable
variable_counts_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(variable_counts),
  N_missing_9999 = as.integer(variable_counts)
)

# 5. Write the summary table at the top of the sheet (row 1)
writeData(
  wb,
  sheet = "Filtered Samples",
  x = summary_table,
  startRow = 1,
  startCol = 1
)

# 6. Write the variable_counts table a bit lower (row 6)
writeData(
  wb,
  sheet = "Filtered Samples",
  x = variable_counts_table,
  startRow = 6,
  startCol = 1
)

# 7. Write the full missing_dat table further down
start_row_missing_dat <- 6 + nrow(variable_counts_table) + 3

writeData(
  wb,
  sheet = "Filtered Samples",
  x = missing_dat,
  startRow = start_row_missing_dat,
  startCol = 1
)

# 8. Save the workbook as an .xlsx file
saveWorkbook(wb, "Omitted_Samples.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## 3. Handling Values Below Detection Limit

Values below detection limits (DL) were handled based on two scenarios:

1.  **Field DL**: calculated as 3 standard deviations above field blank mean value, excluding outlier values
    -   **If concentration \> field DL**: flagged above detection limit (ADL) and retained as-is
    -   **If 0 \< concentrations \< field DL**: flagged below detection limit (BDL) and retained as-is
    -   **If concentration = 0**: flag as ZV and replaced by the lowest reported value of that element
    -   **If concentration \< 0**: flagged as negative (NV) and replaced by the lowest reported value of that element
2.  **Instrument DL**: used for ions that did not have a field DL (i.e. Cl and SO4)
    -   **If concentration \> instrument DL**: flagged above detection limit (ADL) and retained as-is
    -   **If 0 \< concentration \< instrument DL**: flag as BDL and left as-is
    -   **If concentration = 0**: flag as ZV and replace with ½ the instrument DL
    -   **If concentration \< 0**: flagged as negative (NV) and replaced with ½ the instrument DL

The reasoning for omitting 0 and negative values is because

1.  They are likely inaccurate
2.  The BLM cannot handle 0 and negative values

### I. Zinc

Flag and replace the values according to scenario 1 and refer to the Detection Limits tab in WaDE_Synoptic_Summary.xlsx to obtain the field DL value

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Define the field detection limit for Zn in uM
Zn_DL_uM <- 6.69E-02  

# 2. Find the lowest reported positive Zn_uM value
lowest_Zn_uM <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary %>%
  filter(!is.na(Zn_uM), Zn_uM > 0) %>%
  summarise(min_Zn = min(Zn_uM)) %>%
  pull(min_Zn)

lowest_Zn_uM

# 3. Apply detection-limit rules for Zn
WaDE_Synoptic_Summary <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag column for Zn based on your rules
    Zn_flag = case_when(
      Zn_uM < 0 ~ "NV",                       # negative values
      Zn_uM == 0 ~ "ZV",                      # zero values
      Zn_uM > 0 & Zn_uM < Zn_DL_uM ~ "BDL",   # 0 < conc < DL
      Zn_uM >= Zn_DL_uM ~ "ADL"               # ≥ DL = above detection limit
    ),
    
    # Overwrite Zn variable based on your replacement rules
    Zn_uM = case_when(
      Zn_uM < 0 ~ lowest_Zn_uM,           # NV → lowest reported positive Zn
      Zn_uM == 0 ~ lowest_Zn_uM,          # ZV → lowest reported positive Zn
      TRUE ~ Zn_uM                        # BDL and ADL retained as-is
    )
  )

# Inspect all assigned flags
table(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary$Zn_flag, useNA = "ifany")
```

Histogram of measured Zn (uM) with the field DL

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

Zn_DL_uM <- 6.69E-02  # Detection limit

hist_zn <- ggplot(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary, aes(x = Zn_uM)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = Zn_DL_uM),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1,
    color = "red"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Zn Concentrations",
    x = "Zn (uM)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

hist_zn
```

### II. Copper

Flag and replace the values according to scenario 1 and refer to the Detection Limits tab in WaDE_Synoptic_Summary.xlsx to obtain the field DL value

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Define the field detection limit for Zn in uM
Cu_DL_uM <- 2.22E-03 

# 2. Find the lowest reported positive Zn_uM value
lowest_Cu_uM <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary %>%
  filter(!is.na(Cu_uM), Cu_uM > 0) %>%
  summarise(min_Cu = min(Cu_uM)) %>%
  pull(min_Cu)

lowest_Cu_uM

# 3. Apply detection-limit rules for Zn
WaDE_Synoptic_Summary <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag column for Zn based on your rules
    Cu_flag = case_when(
      Cu_uM < 0 ~ "NV",                       # negative values
      Cu_uM == 0 ~ "ZV",                      # zero values
      Cu_uM > 0 & Cu_uM < Cu_DL_uM ~ "BDL",   # 0 < conc < DL
      Cu_uM >= Cu_DL_uM ~ "ADL"               # ≥ DL = above detection limit
    ),
    
    # Overwrite Zn variable based on your replacement rules
    Cu_uM = case_when(
      Cu_uM < 0 ~ lowest_Cu_uM,           # NV → lowest reported positive Zn
      Cu_uM == 0 ~ lowest_Cu_uM,          # ZV → lowest reported positive Zn
      TRUE ~ Cu_uM                        # BDL and ADL retained as-is
    )
  )

# Inspect all assigned flags
table(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary$Cu_flag, useNA = "ifany")
```

### III. Sulfate

Flag and replace the values according to scenario 2 and refer to the README tab in WaDE_Synoptic_Summary.xlsx for the instrument DL value.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Define the instrument DL for sulfate in uM
SO4_DL_uM <- 1.7        
SO4_half_DL_uM <- SO4_DL_uM / 2   # ½ the instrument DL

# 2. Apply detection-limit rules for sulfate
WaDE_Synoptic_Summary <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag column for sulfate
    SO4_flag = case_when(
      is.na(SO4_uM) ~ NA_character_,                # missing
      SO4_uM < 0 ~ "NV",                            # negative values (NV)
      SO4_uM == 0 ~ "ZV",                           # zero values (ZV)
      SO4_uM > 0 & SO4_uM < SO4_DL_uM ~ "BDL",      # 0 < conc < DL (BDL)
      SO4_uM >= SO4_DL_uM ~ "ADL"                   # ≥ DL = above detection limit
    ),
    
    # Adjusted sulfate values
    SO4_uM = case_when(
      SO4_uM < 0 ~ SO4_half_DL_uM,       # NV → replace with ½ instrument DL
      SO4_uM == 0 ~ SO4_half_DL_uM,      # ZV → replace with ½ instrument DL
      TRUE ~ SO4_uM                      # BDL and ADL retained as-is
    )
  )

# Inspect 
table(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary$SO4_flag, useNA = "ifany")
```

Histogram with instrument DL

```{r}
hist_so4 <- ggplot(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary, aes(x = SO4_uM)) +

  ) +

  ) +

    x = "SO4 (uM)",
    y = "Count"

hist_so4
```

### IV. Chloride

Instrument DL: 22.9 uM

```{r}
# 1. Define the instrument detection limit for chloride in uM
Cl_DL_uM <- 2.29e1              # instrument DL = 22.9 uM
Cl_half_DL_uM <- Cl_DL_uM / 2   # ½ the instrument DL

# 2. Apply detection-limit rules for chloride
WaDE_Synoptic_Summary <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag column for chloride
    Cl_flag = case_when(
      Cl_uM < 0 ~ "NV",                           # negative values → NV
      Cl_uM == 0 ~ "ZV",                          # zero values → ZV
      Cl_uM > 0 & Cl_uM < Cl_DL_uM ~ "BDL",       # 0 < conc < DL → BDL
      Cl_uM >= Cl_DL_uM ~ "ADL"                   # ≥ DL = above detection limit
    ),
    
    # Adjusted chloride values
    Cl_uM = case_when(
      Cl_uM < 0 ~ Cl_half_DL_uM,        # NV → replace with ½ instrument DL
      Cl_uM == 0 ~ Cl_half_DL_uM,       # ZV → replace with ½ instrument DL
      TRUE ~ Cl_uM                      # BDL and ADL retained as-is
    )
  )

# Inspect 
table(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary$Cl_flag, useNA = "ifany")
```

## 5. Select BLM Input Variables

Select variables to create separate BLM data inputs for Zn and Cu:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(rlang)

# 1. Create a loop function to create a data frame for any BLM element of choice

create_blm_input <- function(df, metal){

  metal_sym <- sym(metal)

  df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Sample_ID,
      Site,
      Temp_C,
      pH,
      !!metal_sym,
      DOC_uM,
      Ca_uM,
      Mg_uM,
      Na_uM,
      K_uM,
      SO4_uM,
      Cl_uM,
      DIC_uM
    )
}

# 2. Run it for the following trace elements
zn_blm_input_df <- create_blm_input(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary, "Zn_uM")
cu_blm_input_df <- create_blm_input(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary, "Cu_uM")

# 3. Check the results
head(zn_blm_input_df)
head(cu_blm_input_df)
```

Add a column for humic acid at 10 % after DOC

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Zinc
zn_blm_input_df <- zn_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(
    HA = 10 ) %>%
  relocate(HA,  .after = DOC_uM)

# Copper
cu_blm_input_df <- cu_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(
    HA = 10 ) %>%
  relocate(HA, .after = DOC_uM)

# Check
head(zn_blm_input_df)
head(cu_blm_input_df)
```

Add a column for S at the end

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Zinc
zn_blm_input_df <- zn_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate('S_uM' = 1e-10)

# Copper
cu_blm_input_df <- cu_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate('S_uM' = 1e-10)

# Check
summary(zn_blm_input_df$S_uM)
summary(cu_blm_input_df$S_uM)
```

## 4. Unit Conversions

Convert and rewrite trace element units from uM to ug/L

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Zinc
zn_blm_input_df <- zn_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(Zn_uM = Zn_uM * 65.38) %>% # Overwrite Zn (uM) with Zn (ug/L) value
  rename(Zn_ug_L = Zn_uM) # rename AFTER overwriting

# Copper
cu_blm_input_df <- cu_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(Cu_uM = Cu_uM * 63.546) %>% # Overwrite Zn (uM) with Zn (ug/L) value
  rename(Cu_ug_L = Cu_uM) # rename AFTER overwriting

# Check
str(zn_blm_input_df)
str(cu_blm_input_df)
```

Convert DOC, Ca, Mg, Na, K, Cl, SO4, and S from uM to mg/L

```{r}
# Zinc
zn_blm_input_df <- zn_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(
    DOC_uM = DOC_uM * 12.01e-3,
    Ca_uM  = Ca_uM  * 40.078e-3,
    Mg_uM  = Mg_uM  * 24.305e-3,
    Na_uM  = Na_uM  * 22.990e-3,
    K_uM   = K_uM   * 39.098e-3,
    Cl_uM  = Cl_uM  * 35.45e-3,
    SO4_uM = SO4_uM * 96.06e-3,
    S_uM   = S_uM   * 32.06e-3
  ) %>%
  rename(
    DOC_mg_L = DOC_uM,
    Ca_mg_L  = Ca_uM,
    Mg_mg_L  = Mg_uM,
    Na_mg_L  = Na_uM,
    K_mg_L   = K_uM,
    Cl_mg_L  = Cl_uM,
    SO4_mg_L = SO4_uM,
    S_mg_L   = S_uM
  )

# Copper
cu_blm_input_df <- cu_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(
    DOC_uM = DOC_uM * 12.01e-3,
    Ca_uM  = Ca_uM  * 40.078e-3,
    Mg_uM  = Mg_uM  * 24.305e-3,
    Na_uM  = Na_uM  * 22.990e-3,
    K_uM   = K_uM   * 39.098e-3,
    Cl_uM  = Cl_uM  * 35.45e-3,
    SO4_uM = SO4_uM * 96.06e-3,
    S_uM   = S_uM   * 32.06e-3
  ) %>%
  rename(
    DOC_mg_L = DOC_uM,
    Ca_mg_L  = Ca_uM,
    Mg_mg_L  = Mg_uM,
    Na_mg_L  = Na_uM,
    K_mg_L   = K_uM,
    Cl_mg_L  = Cl_uM,
    SO4_mg_L = SO4_uM,
    S_mg_L   = S_uM
  )

# Check
str(zn_blm_input_df)
str(cu_blm_input_df)
```

```{r}

# Zinc
write_xlsx(zn_blm_input_df, "BLM_Data_Entry_for_Zn.xlsx")

# Copper
write_xlsx(cu_blm_input_df, "BLM_Data_Entry_for_Cu.xlsx")
```

## 6. Running the Biotic Ligand Model (BLM)

These two datasets can be used to input into BLM.

Run the following datasets in BLM as follows and name the outputs as follows:

-   Use the **BLM_Data_Entry_for_Zn.xlsx** file to run

    -   BLM as a closed system (DIC input as uM)

        -   BLM in Speciation mode with HA at 10% (output file = Zn Speciation.det)

        -   BLM Speciation mode with HA at 80% (output file = Zn Speciation_ha80.det)

        -   BLM in Toxicity mode for C. dubia (output file = Zn Toxicity on C. dubia.det)

    -   BLM as an open system (no DIC input)

-   Use the **BLM_Data_Entry_for_Cu.xlsx** file to run

    -   BLM as a closed system (DIC input as uM)

        -   BLM in Speciation mode with HA at 10% (output file = Cu Speciation.det)

        -   BLM Speciation mode with HA at 80% (output file = Cu Speciation_ha80.det)

        -   Acute toxicity to C. dubia (output file = Cu Acute Toxicity on P. promelas.det)

        -   Chronic toxicity to C. dubia (output file = Cu Chronic Toxicity on C. dubia.det)

        -   Acute toxicity to P. promelas (output file = Cu Acute Toxicity on C. dubia.det)

        -   Chronic toxicity to P. promelas (output file = Cu Chronic Toxicity on P. promelas.det)

    -   BLM as an open system (no DIC input)

\*Note: make sure that when running BLM with HA at 80% to change this variable and when running BLM as open system to set this mode in BLM (see manual for details).

## 7. Post-Running the BLM

Once the following datasets have been created, follow the steps in 2. Dataset merging.Rmd
